   "theme": "Infrastructure of Poljud and tactical analysis of the Hajduk - Dinamo derby",

    {
     "subtitle": "Water polo conditions and the dilapidated roof of Poljud in a vintage derby",
     "screenshot_description": "Journalists in the Poljud press box protect equipment from leaks while the deluge continues on the pitch.",
     "content": "After a long international break, domestic club football returned in grand fashion with the biggest Croatian derby between Hajduk and Dinamo at Poljud. The match offered a complete spectacle and a comeback by the hosts: Dinamo took the lead through a goal by Dion Drena Beljo, Hajduk swiftly equalized with an own goal, and the final 2:1 was set by Abdoulie Sanyang Bamba at the beginning of the second half. Nevertheless, the final half hour of the encounter was marked by dramatic weather conditions, a deluge, and practically water polo conditions on the waterlogged pitch.\n\nRenato Špehar and Duje Granić reflected on the incredible scenes from the venue. Duje Granić, who followed the match from the stadium together with colleague Marko Štrkalj, emphasized that the derby offered two extremes – top-quality entertainment and a comeback in front of a heated crowd, but also an absurd situation in the press box. Although they were nominally sitting under a roof, journalists had to open umbrellas to protect their laptop computers from leaks. Granić compared the finale of the match to the historic Christmas match between the English and the Germans in the First World War, concluding that football in such chaos was virtually impossible, while the infrastructural shortcomings of Poljud once again surfaced.",

     "subtitle": "Infrastructural problems of Poljud: 'Cosmetics' wasted money or the necessity of a new stadium?",
     "screenshot_description": "Luka Vujić comments on the dilapidated state of the Poljud stands and the question of building a new stadium.",
     "content": "With the revival of the topic of a new stadium at Maksimir, debate regarding the fate of Poljud has reopened in the Split public. While the fans and the club advocate for a modern, new stadium, announcements are arriving from the Government and Prime Minister Andrej Plenković about the renovation of the existing structure. Luka Vujić emphasizes that the downpour during the derby arrived at the ideal moment to expose all the problems of the Poljud beauty, which is in an alarmingly dilapidated state.\n\nVujić cited concrete examples of deterioration: the stairs leading to press and spectator seats are collapsing and being propped up with wooden planks, the entire structure shakes underfoot under heavier load, and the load-bearing columns were at one point tied with wire. In his opinion, any partial 'cosmetic touch-up' of Poljud represents a waste of money, identical to decades of misguided investments in Maksimir. He considers the argument that Poljud is a protected cultural asset to be misguided because that title was acquired primarily to draw European funds that in the end were not adequately utilized. Vujić sees the solution in the construction of a new stadium, even if that means a temporary relocation of Hajduk to a renovated Park mladeži, drawing a parallel with the English who demolished historic structures such as Highbury and the old Wembley without hesitation.",

     "subtitle": "The crazy pressing of Garcia's team brought panic into Dinamo's ranks",
     "screenshot_description": "Display of Hajduk's high pressing structure and the suffocating of Dinamo's back line.",
     "content": "In the tactical analysis of the encounter itself, Marino Durdov pointed out that Hajduk broke Dinamo with an exceptionally aggressive approach, especially at the start of the second half. The hosts came out in high, at moments fanatical pressure that threw the back line of the 'Blues' into total panic and prevented them from calmly playing out from the back. Hajduk's midfield acted compactly and industriously, keeping Dinamo's creative players far away from dangerous areas.\n\nDuje Granić followed up on the analysis of the pressing mechanisms cultivated by coach Gonzalo Garcia. Hajduk's pressing functions such that the wingers press the opposing center-backs, while the full-backs must aggressively step out and close down Dinamo's full-backs. Although there were lapses in communication in the first half – such as the situation on Dinamo's opening goal where three players were watching the throw-in taker and Marušić unnecessarily dropped out of position – Hajduk grew mentally as the match progressed. Granić emphasizes that tactically the derby did not bring revolutionary ideas, but Hajduk's team spirit and unity proved decisive in moments of chaos, confirming Garcia's maxim that it is better to play more poorly and look like a real team than the opposite.",

     "subtitle": "Balance in midfield: Del Moral's running and the solution to Hajduk's long-standing sore spot",
     "screenshot_description": "Graphic depiction of the movement and role of Alberto Del Moral in controlling defensive space.",
     "content": "One of the key factors in Hajduk's victory was finding balance in the center of the pitch. Unlike some past derbies in which the Split team suffered due to a lack of physicality and defensive mobility in the midfield line, the emergence of Alberto Del Moral brought much-needed stability to the position of midfield sweeper. Alongside him, the rest of the midfield gained the freedom for faster and more vertical ball distribution.\n\nLuka Vujić evaluated Del Moral as one of the best individuals on the pitch, right alongside Bamba and Šimun Hrgović. Although the Spaniard is not a technical profile that shines in the final third, his tremendous work ethic, aggressiveness, and coverage of space in front of the back line gave the team a posture that had been missing for years. Vujić and Špehar emphasized that Hajduk now possesses clear profiles – a true 'number six' and 'number eight' – which allows Garcia to assemble a more flexible and physically competitive midfield, without wandering and improvisations with players for whom defensive transition is not a natural role.",

     "subtitle": "Center-back dilemmas and the untamed Racij: Is the risk worth it for the domestic league?",
     "screenshot_description": "Detail of the tactical analysis of center-back movements and reactions of Hajduk's defense.",
     "content": "Despite the celebration, Hajduk's defensive line once again showed certain vulnerabilities, and center-back Racij found himself at the center of the discussion. His performance offered the recognizable 'wild card' pattern: at one moment he unnecessarily leaves Beljo before the opening goal and enters into an ill-advised challenge on Kačavenda that smelled like a red card, while in another phase of the game he dominates in duels and demonstrates enviable physicality.\n\nDuje Granić and Luka Vujić dissected the center-back roster of Split's 'Whites' in detail. While Granić considers that within the HNL framework Racij is currently the first choice at left center-back because his speed and power compensate for shortcomings relative to the competition, Vujić warns of a lack of tactical maturity and poor reading of the game. In situations where Hajduk dominates possession and pushes the back line high, Racij's ability to defend open space and depth is invaluable. However, for European challenges and encounters against stronger opponents like Ajax, Vujić gives preference to tactically more disciplined solutions like Hadžikadunić, emphasizing that in the winter Hajduk must reinforce with another center-back who possesses speed, given that most of the existing center-backs share identical flaws.",

     "subtitle": "Dinamo's right side under scrutiny: Limited full-backs and sterile wingers",
     "screenshot_description": "Tactical display of Dinamo's defensive vulnerability on the flank under pressure from Hajduk.",
     "content": "The biggest surprise in Dinamo's lineup was the inclusion of Pierre-Gabriel on the right flank in tandem with Lisica, which proved to be an extremely ineffective solution. Marino Durdov points out that a full-back brought in with the intention of rotation or 'patching up' after European tests simply does not possess the offensive tools of a modern wide player. In combination with Lisica, who looks for depth and corridors that did not exist at Poljud, Dinamo's right side was completely amputated going forward.\n\nLuka Vujić also pointed to lapses in the defensive phase, noting that Dominguez looks uncertain and that Hajduk deliberately attacked the half-spaces on that side through Bamba. The decision of Mario Kovačević to leave Niko Galešić on the bench, who in the season so far has shown the most defensive stability, is particularly surprising. Analysts agreed that Dinamo skated by on flank positions in the transfer window by bringing in average HNL solutions, which in high-intensity derbies is regularly punished, especially when the contribution of attacking wingers is missing.",

     "subtitle": "Creative drought for the 'Blues': How to replace the Mišić - Stojković axis?",
     "screenshot_description": "Discussion in the studio on the problems of Dinamo's play organization without key midfielders.",
     "content": "Dinamo appeared attack-minded barren at Poljud, creating only one genuine big chance until stoppage time itself. Duje Granić and Marino Durdov see the causes of such helplessness in heavy absences in midfield. In the spring, Dinamo's axis of Josip Mišić – Luka Stojković provided an ideal balance of a classic six, eight, and ten. Without Mišić, who shifts the point of attack with a single move and dictates the tempo, Dinamo had no solutions against Hajduk's compact formation.\n\nReplacement options failed to bring creativity; Kačavenda offers tremendous running energy and aggression in duels, but he lacks composure and vision in the final third, while Marko Zajc is still finding himself this season. Durdov concluded that Dinamo's play relies too heavily on Beljo and set pieces because the wingers do not score goals. The return of Luka Ivanušec imposes itself as a necessity because Dinamo chronically lacks technically superior players who cut into the half-space from the wing and create superiority through combination play, which the classic wingers in Kovačević's system have so far failed to deliver.",

     "subtitle": "Bamba as player of the derby and factor of unpredictability in Garcia's system",
     "screenshot_description": "Luka Vujić analyzes Bamba's tactical role and movement into open space",
     "content": "Following the analysis of the derby's structure, Renato Špehar turns attention to the individual output of Hajduk winger Bamba, who was named player of the match by the show's editorial team. His numbers from the derby were impressive: he scored the winning goal for 2:1, recorded six out of seven successful dribbles, created two big chances, and registered high passing accuracy.\n\nLuka Vujić emphasizes that Bamba essentially has not changed his basic characteristics compared to his arrival in Split; rather, the key lies in the way coach Garcia utilizes him. This is a player who depends on continuity of appearances – this season he has featured in all nine rounds – and Garcia regularly extracts the maximum from wingers. When Bamba gets open space behind the opponent's back line, his speed and penetrativeness in one-on-one play create huge problems for any defense, which was seen against Dinamo, but also earlier against Raków. Vujić adds that Bamba is not the type for complicated combination play in tight spaces, but in transitions and with the adjustments of Del Moral and the back line, he brings exceptional value.\n\nDuje Granić recalls his own earlier criticisms after the match against Žilina, admitting that Bamba goes from one extreme to the other. Due to high emotional sensitivity and a tendency to drop in rhythm, Bamba can string together several unrecognizable matches, but when he has confidence and the coach's trust, he possesses energy and speed that no one else on Hajduk's right wing currently has. Granić underscores that in the derby he made considerably more rational decisions than usual, concluding that with steady focus he can remain Hajduk's most dangerous wing solution.",

     "screenshot_description": "Display of tactical graphic of Hajduk's 3-2-4-1 setup and the role of Šimun Hrgović",
     "content": "The focus of the analysis then shifted to Hajduk's left side and the tactical role of Šimun Hrgović. Duje Granić demonstrates on a graphic display how Hajduk in the buildup phase used a 3-2-4-1 structure (or an asymmetrical 3-2.5) to neutralize Dinamo's high press. In that setup, Hrgović tucked into the center of the pitch or opened up high along the touchline, creating numerical superiority.\n\nParticular emphasis was placed on the outstanding dynamics and fluidity between Hrgović and Šotić. When Hrgović moves into the half-space, Šotić holds the width, and vice versa. Both possess a high work ethic, dynamism, and technical foundation, which is why Granić believes that the left side has become the most dangerous segment of Hajduk's play and that it is no accident that both are being mentioned in the circle of national team candidates.\n\nLuka Vujić followed up by noting that Garcia has turned Hrgović into the prototype of a modern, inverted full-back. Hrgović demonstrated high football intelligence by playing at times as one of the two number sixes, where he reads situations excellently and distributes the ball securely. Although crossing at full sprint is not his forte, his ability to adapt to different roles in the formation makes him one of the players who have progressed the most over the past year.",

     "subtitle": "Psychological step forward in the downpour and evaluation of referee Igor Pajač",
     "screenshot_description": "Luka Vujić speaks about the psychological barrier and Hajduk's winning mentality",
     "content": "Analyzing the finale of the match in water polo conditions at Poljud, the interlocutors touched upon the psychological state of the Split team. Luka Vujić underscores that in the past it regularly happened that Hajduk faltered in dramatic finishes under a heavy downpour, but this team shows an entirely different posture. The victory against Dinamo – Garcia's first in derbies – alongside the earlier progression in Europe against Raków, shows that the squad has broken through a psychological barrier and built faith in its own capabilities even when finding itself trailing on the scoreboard.\n\nRenato Špehar then opens the question of the officiating of head referee Igor Pajač. The derby offered several contentious situations, including a dangerous challenge by Kačavenda on Del Moral that went without a booking, a risky challenge by Rači, as well as an unusual episode with a potential stoppage in stoppage time in the 95th minute.\n\nMarino Durdov rates Pajač's officiating as passable, pointing out that in derbies the referee regularly relies on compensating decisions. Although he considers that Kačavenda had to receive a card and Rači's tackle was on the verge of a sending-off, Durdov concludes that in the end the referee did not directly determine the winner, which in a derby with such tensions and weather conditions is the most important thing. He assessed the confusion over stopping the match due to pyrotechnics in the final minutes as an unnecessary circus that only watered down an already chaotic finish.",

     "subtitle": "Poljud spectacle against Ajax: Hajduk at the opening of the Conference League",
     "screenshot_description": "Duje Granić explains why Hajduk must not retreat into a bunker against Ajax",
     "content": "The derby was merely the prelude to a hellish 15 days with five matches for both rivals. For Hajduk, a European spectacle follows – the opening of the league phase of the Conference League against Dutch giant Ajax at a sold-out Poljud. Renato Špehar shared his observations after watching Ajax live against Excelsior, noting that the team under new management has not yet reached its full peak and suffers from problems in defensive transition, but individual quality and physicality in attack will present a huge challenge for the Split defense.\n\nDuje Granić highlights the fantastic atmosphere expected in the stands and appeals for Hajduk not to change its identity. He believes that retreating into a bunker and switching to a 5-4-1 would be a cardinal error because the team does not have the profiles for passive defending in a low block. Hajduk must play bravely, press the Dutch carried by the support from the stands, and seek their chances, without fear of an eventual defeat.\n\nLuka Vujić agreed with that thesis, recalling that Ajax, which was taken over by Michel (former coach of Girona), is the most powerful opponent in terms of players to arrive at Poljud since the clash with Villarreal. Despite departures of key individuals, Ajax possesses top names such as Amrabat and Marcos Leonardo. Vujić concludes that Hajduk has nothing to lose in this encounter, and the fact that tickets sold out in just 50 minutes speaks sufficiently of the euphoria prevailing after 15 years of waiting for a European autumn.",

     "subtitle": "Dinamo facing a challenge in Brussels: Can Kovačević break Anderlecht?",
     "screenshot_description": "Marino Durdov analyzes the play and profile of Belgian Anderlecht",
     "content": "Parallel to Hajduk's test, Dinamo faces a difficult away match in Brussels against Anderlecht within the Europa League. Marino Durdov draws a parallel with last season's clashes against Genk, describing Anderlecht as an exceptionally fast, vertical, and combinative team that insists on penetrating the opponent's penalty area and scores all its goals in the domestic championship inside the 16-meter box.\n\nFor Dinamo it will be a massive tactical test, especially after the uncertainties shown in the derby by center-backs McKenna and Dominguez. Durdov expects Galešić's return to the starting lineup, either at center-back or full-back position, in order to solidify defensive stability. Going forward, Dinamo will depend on the return and inspiration of Stojković and the awakening of the wingers, who recently have not been providing the expected contribution.\n\nAfter the test in Belgium, Dinamo returns to domestic commitments against Slaven Belupo, which Durdov sees as an ideal opportunity to catch league rhythm before the continuation of a congested schedule and the future derby with Rijeka. Renato Špehar concludes the broadcast with an announcement of a new analysis immediately after European Thursday, when it will be clearer how the Croatian representatives passed their first continental tests.",
